title: Engineering Molecular Recognition with Bio-mimetic Polymers on Single Walled Carbon Nanotubes
protocol: Dissolve 584 mg of NaCl in 80 mL of deionized water.
Add deionized water to bring total volume to 100 mL for 100 mM NaCl solution preparation.
Dissolve 3 g of SDS in 80 mL of deionized water.
Add deionized water to bring total volume to 100 mL for 3% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) solution preparation.
Dissolve 2 g of sodium cholate hydrate in 80 mL of deionized water.
Add deionized water to bring total volume to 100 mL for 2% sodium cholate (SC) solution preparation.
Dissolve 22.23 g of Tris base and 58.44 g of NaCl in 500 mL of deionized water using a magnetic stir bar and plate.
Carefully add concentrated HCl until a pH of 8.1 is reached for imaging buffer preparation (1x Tris: 20 mM Tris, 100 mM NaCl).
Add deionized water to reach a final volume of 1 L for imaging buffer preparation.
Dissolve amine difunctionalized polyethylene glycol (PEG) and rhodamine isothiocyanate (RITC) in 1 mL of a 1:1 mixture of dichloromethane and dimethylformamide (DMF).
Add 0.2 mol/L of N,N-diisopropylethylamine (DIEA).
Precipitate the mixture with 10x volume of diethyl ether followed by vacuum filtration.
Redissolve in DMF and repeat ether precipitation followed by vacuum filtration.
Combine 100 µL of Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine hydrochloride (TCEP) solution (0.5 M, pH 7.0) with 44.9 µL of 5'-thiol-modified DNA (1 mg/10 µL in 0.1 M NaCl).
Add the mixture to 4.855 mL of deionized water and stir for 1 h.
Dissolve 500 mg of methoxypolyethylene glycol maleimide in 5 mL of phosphate buffered saline.
Combine DNA and PEG solutions (10 mL total) and stir for 24 h.
Add 200-300 mg of unwashed SWNTs into a plastic centrifuge tube containing 45 mL of deionized water.
Vortex the solution for 2 min.
Sonicate using a bath sonicator for 5 min.
Centrifuge the solution for 20 min at 16,100 x g and discard supernatant.
Add approximately 45 mL of fresh deionized water to the pellet.
Repeat steps 2.1.2-2.1.4 up to 8 times.
Remove as much water as possible from the SWNT pellet without disturbing it and allow the SWNT pellet to air dry.
Dissolve nucleic acids (NA) in 0.1 M NaCl to a concentration of 100 mg/mL.
Remove static electricity from disposable spatula, microcentrifuge tubes, and SWNT stock using an anti-static gun.
Add 20 μL of the NA solution to 980 μL of 0.1 M NaCl followed by the addition of 1 mg SWNTs in a fume hood.
Sonicate the solution for 10 min at 40% amplitude with an ultrasonicator using a 3 mm diameter tip, in an ice bath.
Centrifuge the DNA-SWNT solution twice for 90 min at 16,100 x g.
If using PEG-DNA, purify out excess and unreacted DNA and PEG using a 100 kDa spin-filter.
Add enough PBS to fill the spin-filter and spin at 9,300 x g for 1.5 min.
Repeat this wash step three times.
Collect and keep the supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet containing CNT bundles and aggregates.
Discard the pellet according to institutional hazardous waste procedures appropriate for nanomaterials.

Measure the solution absorbance at 632 nm using a UV/Vis spectrophotometer to determine approximate concentration of suspended SWNTs using ε=0.036 L/cm·mg in accordance with Lambert-Beer's law and the appropriate dilution factor.
Remove static electricity from disposable spatula, micro centrifuge tubes, and SWNT stock.
Add 5 mg of SWNTs to 5 mL of a 2% SC solution in a fume hood.
Sonicate the solution for 1 hour at 40% amplitude using an ultrasonicator with a 6 mm diameter tip in an ice bath.
Centrifuge the sample at 150,000 x g for 4 hours using an ultracentrifuge and carefully collect the supernatant.
Dissolve 1 wt % of amphiphilic polymer (e.g., RITC-PEG-RITC) in the SC-SWNT solution.
Dialyze the polymer-SC-SWNT solution against 1 L of deionized water or buffer using a 3.5 kDa dialysis membrane for 5 days, changing out the water or buffer after hour 2 and hour 4.
Measure the absorbance of the solution at 632 nm using a UV/Vis spectrophotometer to determine the approximate concentration of suspended SWNTs.
Dissolve 10 mg lyophilized BSA-biotin in 1 mL deionized water to make a stock solution and store it at 4 °C.
Dissolve 10 mg NeutrAvidin protein (NAV) in 2 mL of deionized water to make a stock solution and store aliquots at -20 °C.
Clean a microscope slide with deionized water.
Clean a microscope slide with methanol.
Clean a microscope slide with acetone.
Rinse the microscope slide with deionized water.
Place several pieces of double-sided tape approximately 5 mm apart on the clean microscope slide to create channels.
Take a long glass coverslip and press it onto the top of the double-sided tape, ensuring it is centered on the microscope slide.
Add 100 µL of BSA-Biotin stock solution to 900 µL of 1x Tris buffer to achieve a final concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Flow 50 µL of the BSA-biotin solution into the channel by pipetting the solution into one end and wicking away solution at the other using a tissue.
Incubate for 5 minutes.
Flush the channel with 3-5 flushes of 50 µL of 0.1 M NaCl.
Dilute 40 µL of 5 mg/mL NAV stock in 960 µL 1x Tris buffer to achieve a final concentration of 0.2 mg/mL.
Flow 50 µL of the NAV solution into the channel by pipetting the solution into one end and wicking away solution at the other using a tissue.
Incubate for 2-5 minutes.
Flush the channel with 3-5 flushes of 50 µL of 0.1 M NaCl.
Dilute stock solutions of suspended SWNTs in imaging buffer to a concentration of 1-10 mg/L.
Flow 50 µL of the diluted SWNT solution into the channel and incubate for 5 minutes.
Gently rinse away excess SWNTs using 50 µL of imaging buffer.
Prepare a 10% solution of (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES) in ethanol.
Flow 100 µL of 1x Tris buffer into the channel.
Flush the channel with APTES solution and incubate for 5 min.
Wash the channel with 1x Tris buffer.
Dilute stock solutions of suspended DNA-SWNTs in imaging buffer to a concentration of 1-10 mg/L.
Flow 50 µL of the diluted DNA-SWNT solution into the channel and incubate for 5 min.
Gently rinse away excess SWNTs using 50 µL of imaging buffer.
Direct the laser beam to enter the back illumination port of an inverted microscope using mirrors on adjustable kinematic mounts.
Place a pair of post-mounted irises set to the port height in the path of the beam.
Confirm that the beam passes through both irises when placed between subsequent mirrors and before it enters the illumination port.
Adjust the beam height using a periscope assembly if necessary.
Remove any short-pass heat filters on the illumination port that would attenuate the beam.
Insert an appropriate filter cube into the microscope to reflect excitation light into the objective and collect emission light.
Ensure the dichroic long pass filter in the cube has a cutoff above the excitation wavelength (e.g., 750 LP).
Choose an emission long pass filter (e.g., 850 LP) to further minimize scattered excitation light from hitting the sensor.
Select an emission filter that is specific for the emission of SWNTs with a particular chirality if required.
Perform fine adjustments to the beam alignment by inserting an appropriate alignment cube replacing the objective.
Use two offset, frosted discs containing 1 mm pinholes in the alignment cube.
Align the beam to the center of both the lower and upper alignment discs.
Attach a 2D InGaAs sensor array to the side imaging port of the microscope using an appropriate adapter.
Use a 0.5X lens if necessary to accommodate the size of the sensor.
Apply fluorescence-free immersion oil on the sample using a 100X oil immersion objective (1.4 NA).
Place the immobilized SWNT sample onto the microscope stage.
Raise the objective until the oil contacts the bottom of the cover glass (#1.5, 170 µm thickness).
Adjust the objective collar if necessary for imaging conditions.
Slowly raise the objective with the excitation source on and monitor the fluorescence signal of the InGaAs camera.
Direct the collected light out of the microscope body and into a spectrometer using kinematic mounts and mirrors rated for nIR.
Focus the light down to a point onto the entrance slit using a focusing lens (e.g., plano-convex, f = 150 mm).
Attenuate the laser power to <1 mW and replace the microscope objective with a 1" mirror and use a 50/50 beam-splitting filter cube.
Adjust the mirrors and lens to focus the beam onto the entrance slit.
Place a well plate onto the microscope stage.
Record the spectra of an in-focus sample using the spectrometer and InGaAs array.
Mount sensor-coated channels onto the microscope stage.
Bring into focus using a 100X oil objective and InGaAs camera.
Add 50 µL of 100 µM dopamine solution in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to the flow channel.
Record the change in fluorescence intensity.
Wash out the dopamine solution using phosphate buffered saline.
Observe the change in fluorescence of individual SWNT sensors.
Pipette equal volumes of suspended SWNT sensor into each well, typically >100 µL for a 96-well plate and >30 µL for a 384-well plate.
Pipette analytes from screening library into the well plates in triplicate.
Raise the objective while monitoring the emission spectra using the spectrometer and InGaAs array.
Record a 1-10 s exposure for each sample well to collect a spectrum.
Compare the emission spectra for each well to a control containing just SWNTs without additional analyte to quantify the fluorescence response.
